## Three systems, one economy {.theme-content}

- **Energy statistics** describe the supply and use of energy products on the territory, by technical sector (the energy balance of ONEM).
- **Greenhouse gas inventories** describe emissions on the territory, by process (the inventory coordinated by ANME).
- **National accounts** describe the economy of resident units, by industry, in money (the supply and use tables of the INS).

The System of Environmental-Economic Accounting (SEEA) connects the three [@seea2014].

## What the SEEA adds

- The **same units and classifications** as the national accounts: 24 industries, households, the rest of the world.
- **Physical supply and use tables**, in which every flow has a supplier and a user, and supply equals use.
- The **residence principle**: what resident units do, wherever they do it.
- Indicators that relate physical flows to output, value added and consumption.

## The accounts covered here

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Physical energy flow accounts (PEFA)**

Energy from natural inputs, energy products and energy residuals, in terajoules, by industry and households [@seeaenergy2019; @eurostat2014pefa].
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Air emissions accounts (AEA)**

Greenhouse gases emitted by industries and households, in tonnes of CO2 equivalent, reconciled with the inventory by a bridge table [@eurostat2015aea].
:::
::::

## Energy flows in the SEEA

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  ENV1["Environment"] -- "natural inputs" --> IND["Resident industries"]
  ROW1["Rest of the world"] -- "imports" --> IND
  IND -- "energy products" --> HH["Households"]
  IND -- "exports" --> ROW2["Rest of the world"]
  IND -- "residuals" --> ENV2["Environment"]
  HH -- "residuals" --> ENV2
```

Energy is conserved: every use of energy returns to the environment as a residual of the same size [@seeaenergy2019, paras 2.14 to 2.21].

## What the accounts make possible

- Energy and emissions **per dinar of value added**, by industry.
- The share of **households** in energy use and emissions, and its components.
- Consistent inputs for **economic models** and climate policy analysis.
- International comparison with the same concepts as other countries.
